title: Oncall Tactical Summary — Week Aug 10–16, 2026
content:
Purpose: quick tactical digest for SRE on-call + infra leads. Aim is to capture: incidents, SLO health, immediate mitigations, outstanding follow-ups, and handoff notes for the next shift. Lightweight — action items prioritized first.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Two notable incidents this week: (A) transient 5xx spike hitting hosted inference front-door due to a stale KV-cache compaction bug, (B) autoscaler oscillation in the model-serving pool causing degraded throughput to Dedicated customers for ~18 minutes.
- SLOs: 99.95% p99 latency (30s window) currently at 99.82% for the week; error budget burned ~0.13% (elevated by incident A).
- Immediate fixes deployed and validated; follow-ups assigned. No P1s remain open.

1) Incident A — KV-cache compaction race (Aug 11 03:12 UTC)
- Symptoms: sudden increase in 500s returned from front-door service, primarily for requests with long prefixes (seq len > 2048). Error rate peaked at 4.2% for 8 minutes.
- Root cause hypothesis: recent compaction PR (runtime#981) introduced an off-by-one in compaction epoch handling; older KV entries that were expected to be present returned empty leading to unhandled null deref in the prefetch layer.
- Timeline (short):
  - 03:12 - Pager triggered (oncall: Tom). 03:15 - Bridge opened.
  - 03:18 - Initial mitigation: toggled read-through fallback flag to avoid strict cache-only path (config flag: KV_PREFETCH_STRICT=false). Error rate dropped to 0.6%.
  - 03:33 - Full rollback of runtime#981 to previous release; error rate returned to baseline by 03:40.
- Impact: Hosted API availability SLO degraded on that 8-minute window; estimated customer-facing errors ~3,700 requests.
- Short-term mitigations applied: 1) Read-through fallback (as above), 2) Added a temporary health-check on compaction agent to stop compaction while older-format entries exist, 3) Increased KV cache instrumentation (traces + histograms) to catch missing-key incidents.
- Owners: remediation/rollback (Tom Becker), follow-up root-cause investigation (Carlos Alvarez), QA guardrails (Aisha Khan).
- Follow-ups:
  - CAR (Corrective Action Report) draft in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/KV-Cache-Incident-2026-08 (Carlos, due 2026-08-19).
  - Add unit+integration tests for compaction epoch boundaries in runtime repo (PR referenced above). (Carlos/Tom, due 2026-08-18).
  - Add a canary compaction step that runs on <1% of nodes before global rollout. (Aisha, proposal due 2026-08-20).

2) Incident B — Autoscaler oscillation (Aug 13 14:02 UTC)
- Symptoms: model-serving autoscaler rapidly scaled down then back up several times due to a feedback loop between the cheap-evict heuristic and the burst-provisioning policy. During oscillation throughput dropped ~22% for 18 minutes for a Dedicated customer region.
- Timeline (short):
  - 14:02 - Pager escalated to SRE lead (Priya). 14:08 - Identified autoscaler decision churn in metrics.
  - 14:12 - Temporary change: increased min_replicas for affected pool from 6 -> 8. This stabilized throughput.
  - 14:20 - Deployed autoscaler policy tweak to include a hold-down window (120s) to prevent immediate downsizing after a scale-up.
- Root cause: tuning regression shipped in autoscaler policy v2.7 that set aggressiveness too high for certain bursty workloads.
- Impact: Dedicated SLAs remained within grace (customer ticket opened; CS notified).
- Follow-ups:
  - Revert aggressive default and add traffic-profile-based policy selection. (Infra-autoscale team, owner: Mei Chen, due 2026-08-21).
  - Post-incident sim: run autoscaler against recorded production traces for 72h window to validate. (Tom/Aisha, due 2026-08-22).

3) SLO snapshot and error budget
- SLOs tracked this week (rolling 7d windows unless noted):
  - Hosted inference availability (HTTP 2xx or 3xx): target 99.99% — current 99.95% (7d) — error budget remaining: 0.04%
  - P99 request latency target < 1200ms for small prompts: target 99.9% — current 99.6% (7d) — significant pressure from KV-cache incident
  - Dedicated throughput SLA: target 99.5% — currently 99.48% (7d) — minor burn due to autoscaler event
- Action: escalate SLO review in next SRE sync; propose a temporary SLO alert adjustment to reduce pager noise if we accept short corrective windows. (Priya to propose change; decision meeting 2026-08-18).

4) On-call handoffs and staffing notes
- This week shifts: Aug 10–16 schedule attached (Tom, Aisha, Mei, Priya rotating).
- Handoff template reminder: include 1) outstanding incidents + status, 2) config flags touched, 3) ongoing experiments that interact with runtime (e.g. canary compaction), 4) any planned maintenance. Please post handoff notes to #sre-handoffs.
- Notable: two overlapping canary experiments are scheduled next week (quantization rollout + cache compaction canary). Recommend one-at-a-time to reduce blast radius. (Action: Product infra to re-sequence. Owner: Sarah Lim, due 2026-08-17).

5) Runbook and observability changes (quick wins implemented this week)
- Added a KV-cache-specific health endpoint and Prometheus exporter metrics for compaction epochs (merged runtime PR#983).
- Added a Grafana dashboard panel to surface read-miss spikes by prefix length (dashboard id: SRE-KV-08).
- Pager thresholds adjusted: KV-cache read-error alert increased sensitivity to 0.5% for 5m windows; will monitor false positives for 72h.

6) Action items (prioritized)
- High priority (P0/P1):
  - Complete compaction epoch unit tests + merge PR (Carlos) — due 2026-08-18.
  - Draft CAR and postmortem (Tom/Carlos) — due 2026-08-19.
  - Autoscaler policy revert + simulation tests (Mei/Tom) — due 2026-08-21.
- Medium priority:
  - Canary compaction design doc (Aisha) — due 2026-08-20.
  - Update handoff template to include active experiments list (Priya) — due 2026-08-16.
- Low priority:
  - Add a synthetic canary for Dedicated throughput in eu-west region (SRE infra) — due 2026-09-01.

7) Known risks and open questions
- Risk: two infrastructure experiments may interact (quantization rollout and compaction canary) — need explicit sequencing.
- Question: should we temporarily tighten SLO alert windows to reduce noise or loosen to avoid pagers while we stabilize? (Proposal scheduled 2026-08-18).
- Risk: increased observability retention for KV traces will raise costs — need product/finance signoff for extended retention for 30d vs default 7d. (Finance flagged; budget meeting 2026-08-19).

8) Notes to self / rough ideas
- Consider adding a lightweight preflight checker that validates compaction invariants on canary node before rolling. Could be run as a CI job on runtime images.
- Would be useful to correlate model-serving throttles with specific model-version deployments — add labels into autoscaler metrics for model_id.

9) Handoff for next shift (Aug 13 20:00 UTC)
- Primary: monitor KV-cache error-rate panel and autoscaler oscillation metric (metric ids: kv.cache.read_errors.pct, autoscale.churn.rate).
- No ongoing P1s. Watch for CAR review meeting prep.
- Contact list: Priya Menon (sre-lead), Tom Becker (oncall), Carlos Alvarez (runtime), Aisha Khan (observability).

Appendix (quick links):
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/981
- Confluence incident draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/KV-Cache-Incident-2026-08
- Jira: SRE-4127, INC-2026-08-11-01

-- end --

(Edited quick notes; will expand CAR with timelines and packet captures for postmortem.)
